chunks: And by this chain, from Muḥammad ibn Zayd, who said:
A group from Khurāsān came to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام and asked him to release them from the khums.
So he said: “How barren this is! You profess pure affection for us with your tongues, yet you withhold from us a right that Allah has appointed for us and has assigned us to it, and it is the khums.”
“We do not make it lawful, we do not make it lawful, we do not make it lawful for any one of you.”

key_terms.الْخُمُسِ: khums, the one-fifth due designated as a divinely ordained financial right
key_terms.جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ لَنَا: Allah appointed it for us as our due
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: in a state of release or exemption from liability

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام permit people to be exempted from khums?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام refused to exempt a group from Khurāsān from paying khums. He states that khums is a right appointed by Allah for the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, and he strongly rejects verbal claims of loyalty that are not matched by fulfilling this financial obligation. The narration highlights the binding nature of khums and the seriousness of withholding divinely assigned rights.
